verses.1: The message that came to Jeremias from Jehovah in the twelfth year of Jehoiada, king of Judah, was this: It was the year in which twelve years had passed since Nebukadnezar’s reign.
verses.2: And then the army of King Babylon attacked Jerusalem. And Jeremiah, the prophet, was in the palace of the king of Judah at that time.
verses.3: And they said to King Jehoshaphat, “Do you know that you will be taken captive? For thus says the LORD: ‘I will give this city into the hands of King Babylon.’”
verses.4: And Zedekiah, king of Judah, will not be captured by the enemies. For he was given into the hands of King Babylon. His words are heard through his mouth, and his eyes are seen with his own eyes.
verses.5: And Babylon will go forth with its warriors. There, it will be destroyed by God’s judgment. For they will not succeed in fighting against those who are evil.
verses.6: And Jeremiah said, “This is what the LORD said to me.”
verses.7: Look, Hanamel, son of Shalum, your debtor, has come to you and said, “Buy me back my field that was taken from me in the lawsuit.” For it is your right to have it back.
verses.8: And Hananiah son of Dodai came to me, as the Lord commanded. He went into the courtyard of the palace and said to me, “Please buy my field that is located in the land of Benjamin. It belongs to you, as it was given to you by the judge. You can take it for yourself.” Then I knew that this was indeed the word of the Lord.
verses.9: And I will take the money from Hanamel, son of Delain. He was the one who gave it to me in exchange for my prayers. I will give him seven shekels and twelve homers as payment.
verses.10: And I will write it down in the book, and I will gather the witnesses together. Then I will take the money into my ears.
verses.11: And I will take the book of ordinances, along with its markings and laws, as well as the regulations.
verses.12: And I will give the register of those who were registered to Baruch, son of Neriah, son of Mahziah, for the eyes of Hananiah, my father, and for the eyes of all the Jews who live in the palace of the ruler.
verses.13: And I will command that blessed one to be seen by them.
verses.14: As Jehovah, the army of heaven and God of Israel, said: “Take these registers—the register of those who were bought, the register of those who were enslaved, and the register of those who were released. Place them in a chest, so that many days will pass before they are used.”
verses.15: For as Jehovah, the army of Israel’s God, says, “They will still build houses, fields, and vineyards in this land.”
verses.16: And I will pray to the LORD after I have counted the items that were purchased. May they be blessed, O son of Neriya.
verses.17: Ah, Adonai Yehovah! Look, you have created the heavens and the earth with your great power. Nothing can fall from your hands.
verses.18: He does mercy for the thousands; he forgives the sins of their fathers. After them, there is the great and powerful God, Jehovah, with His armies.
verses.19: Great is your wisdom, and abundant are your plans! Your eyes see all the ways of human beings. You decide for people according to their own ways and do whatever pleases you.
verses.20: You who have set up idols and graven images in the land of Egypt, until today. In Israel as well as among men, you will be given a name today.
verses.21: And your people, Israel, went out of Egypt in great numbers, with strong arms, and with a mighty army.
verses.22: And she gave them this land, which you promised to their ancestors that they would receive as a gift: land covered with milk and honey.
verses.23: And they came and took her away. But they did not listen to your voice or follow your commands. They did not do everything that you commanded them to do. So, I will call upon all these evils against them.
verses.24: Look, those invaders came to take control of the city. The city was given into the hands of those who fought against it, due to destruction, famine, and other disasters. And you see what happened.
verses.25: And you said to me, “O Adonai YHWH, give me the field in exchange for money. The city will be given into the hands of the captors.”
verses.26: And the words of Jehovah were spoken to Jeremias, “Thus says Jehovah.”
verses.27: Behold, I, Jehovah, the God of all flesh, will bring down to earth everything that rises against me.
verses.28: Therefore, Jehovah said, “I will give this city into the hands of the enemies and into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.”
verses.29: And those wicked warriors came against this city. They set fire to the city and burned it down. They also destroyed all the houses that were built on its rooftops. They sacrificed animals to other gods, just to provoke me further.
verses.30: For the children of Israel and the children of Judah do evil in my eyes. They commit wrong against their own daughters. But the children of Israel still angered me with their actions. But LORD, they still do evil in my sight.
verses.31: For on my forehead and in my temples, this city has been a source of great joy for me ever since I built it. But until today, it remains on my forehead.
verses.32: On all the evil deeds of the children of Israel and of the Jews, who caused me harm. Their kings, their priests, their prophets, and all the people of Judah and Jerusalem also did evil deeds.
verses.33: And they turned to me with their backs turned, and they did not listen to my teachings. They were ignorant and refused to learn.
verses.34: And they placed their containers in the room whose name was “Shimi”.
verses.35: And they built the altars for the king, in the valley of Ben-Hinnom, so that they could burn their children and their wives as sacrifices to the king. They were not commanded to do this, and it never entered my mind to do such a thing, just to deceive the Jews.
verses.36: And now, as Jehovah, the God of Israel, says: To this city, which you say has been given into the hands of King Babylon during times of famine, plague, and war.
verses.37: I am brought forth from all the lands where they were rejected, in pain and suffering, with great heat and torment. They are brought back to this place, and settled in safety.
verses.38: And I will be their God.
verses.39: And I will give them one heart and one way, so that they may always serve me for their own good. And their hearts will follow mine.
verses.40: And I made a covenant with them for ever. I will not turn away from them again to harm them or destroy them. My love will be in their hearts forever, without any doubt.
verses.41: And I hope to improve them, and to plant them in this land with all my heart and soul.
verses.42: For as Jehovah said, when I brought all this great evil upon this people, so also I will bring to them all the good that I have spoken about them.
verses.43: And the field was acquired in this land, which you say is “empty” from any people or animals. It was given into the hands of the conquerors.
verses.44: They will be bought with money; their names will be written in the records. They will be witnesses on earth, in the regions around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hills, in the cities of the lowlands, and in the cities of the Negev. May Jehovah restore their freedom, as it is written.
